qwen.ref_text: On the battlefield, four players with monster-like strength appeared. Each of the players had already destroyed their colonies. These players were so equally strong, they created a four-way deadlock.

lines: Algorithms, phase one. Foundations and PageRank. This is how Google ranked the web.
Find the biggest number is only a wish. It does not say how.
“Find the biggest” is only a wish.
An algorithm settles the input, the steps, the comparison, the stopping point and the output in advance.
An algorithm answers every question in advance.
For an empty list, we decide in advance that the answer is none.
Even: what if the list is empty?
The loop scans once, and keeps the biggest number so far.
Scan once and keep the biggest so far.
After any number of items, best is the biggest of those items.
After k items, best is the biggest of those k.
A green tick shows the promise still holds after every step. That is the loop invariant.
It stays true after every step: the invariant.
At the end, the promise is the answer. It is nine.
At the end the promise is the answer: 9.
Each square is one call of work. With n equal to eight, one loop makes eight.
Each square is one work() call. One loop: 8.
The inner loop grows, making a staircase. Zero plus one plus two, up to seven, is twenty-eight.
The inner loop grows: 0 + 1 + 2 + … + 7 = 28.
Let it run to n instead, and every square fills. Eight times eight is sixty-four.
Let it run to n instead: 8 × 8 = 64.
Halving goes eight, four, two, one. That is only three calls.
Halving: 8, 4, 2, 1 is only 3 calls.
Now double n, from eight to sixteen.
Now double n, from 8 to 16.
One loop does twice the work. That is big O of n.
One loop: twice the work.
Nested loops do four times the work. That is big O of n squared.
Nested loops: four times the work.
The growing inner loop goes from twenty-eight to one hundred and twenty, about four times more.
Growing inner loop: 28 to 120, about ×4.
Halving gains just one call. That is big O of log n.
Halving: just one extra call.
The shape of the growth is the big O.
The shape of the growth is the Big-O.
Pages link to pages. Circles are pages, and arrows are links.
Pages link to pages.
Give every page twenty-five tokens of rank, one hundred in all.
Give every page 25 tokens of rank.
Each page pours its tokens equally down its links.
Each page pours its tokens down its links.
Page D has no links, so its twenty-five tokens vanish. The total drops to seventy-five.
D has no links, so its 25 tokens vanish.
The fix is that a dead end pours to every page, six and a quarter each.
Fix: a dead end pours to every page.
Now nothing is lost, and the total is one hundred again.
Now nothing is lost: the total is 100 again.
Now A and B link only to each other. Nobody links to X.
A and B link only to each other.
The rank sloshes between A and B, round after round.
Rank sloshes between them, round after round.
X is starved, while A and B just swap the lead.
X is starved; A and B just swap the lead.
Suppose the rank could jump to any page.
What if the rank could jump anywhere?
A surfer follows a random link, eighty-five per cent of the time.
The surfer follows a link 85% of the time.
Otherwise, it teleports to a random page.
Otherwise it teleports to a random page.
Now count the visits over six hundred hops.
Count the visits over many hops.
The shares settle. A gets forty-nine per cent and B forty-six. That is the PageRank.
The shares settle: that is PageRank.
X is no longer starved. It gets five per cent, just from teleporting.
X is no longer starved: 5%, by teleporting.
Now the web is a table. Each column shows where one page sends its rank.
Each column is where one page sends its rank.
T has no links, so its column sums to zero. We fill it with a fifth each.
T's column sums to 0, so T pours 0.2 to all.
For teleporting, multiply by zero point eight five, then add a floor of zero point zero three.
Teleport: × 0.85, then add 0.15 ÷ 5 = 0.03.
Start with the same rank on every page, a fifth each.
Start with equal rank on every page.
Each round, multiply the ranks by the matrix.
Each round: multiply by the matrix.
Early rounds swing a lot, then the ranks settle down.
Early rounds swing, then the ranks settle.
Page R ranks first. The same loop can rank billions of pages.
R ranks first. The same loop ranks billions.
A loop is correct when its promise stays true.
Double the input, and the work grows times two, times four, or plus one.
Share rank, teleport, and repeat until the ranks settle.
